tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on Lighting and Flash

questions.question: Create a series of experimental studies exploring lighting and flash. Annotate your process.
questions.correctAnswer: A range of experimental studies showing different approaches to lighting and flash, each annotated with media, technique and purpose. Show development from initial experiments to refined outcomes.

questions.question: Research an artist or designer who works with lighting and flash. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed your own work.
questions.correctAnswer: A critical analysis naming a specific artist/designer, using specialist vocabulary, explaining their context and approach, and making clear connections to personal work.

questions.question: Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with lighting and flash. Which approaches were most successful and why?
questions.correctAnswer: A reflective evaluation identifying successful and less successful experiments, explaining WHY using technical and conceptual language, and showing how evaluation led to further refinement.

tests.name: Extended Practice
tests.description: Self-marked extended answers on Lighting and Flash

questions.question: Full-Mark Response Photograph the same subject using at least three different lighting setups (e.g. natural side light, backlit silhouette, diffused window light). Annotate each describing the light quality, direction and mood created. <div class="
questions.correctAnswer: A grade 9 response will: demonstrate understanding of light direction and quality; use at least three different lighting approaches; annotate with specialist vocabulary (hard/soft light, colour temperature, rim lighting, key light, fill); explain how lighting choices create mood and meaning. Mark scheme: AO1 (develop through investigation) + AO2 (refine through experimentation) + AO3 (record ideas and observations) + AO4 (present personal response) = total marks
questions.explanation: Extended answer: aim for the mark-scheme points, in order, with the command word addressed.
